evidence_updates.update: AutoResearchClaw independently supports the broader failure-recovery family but not SAGE's specific multi-hypothesis attribution mechanism. In a best-of-3 component ablation over the same 10 ARC-Bench topics, removing Self-Healing reduced manuscript completion from 10/10 to 6/10 and selected-output quality from 5.62 to 4.83; combined removal of Debate and Self-Healing fell to 4/10 completion, quality 3.47, and 0 accepted outputs. This is direct evidence that iterative runtime repair can be a completion-critical mechanism, while causal credit for multi-hypothesis diagnosis remains specific to SAGE.

MLReplicate's abstract says the cheapest system outperformed the most resource-intensive system despite a 38-fold difference in input tokens. The detailed resource section does not support that token ratio: CycleResearcher uses 8.1K input tokens versus AI Researcher 6.80M, about 840x; AI Researcher versus Agent Laboratory is about 10.9x and versus Tiny Scientist about 18.5x. The reported monetary cost ratio $17.72/$0.46 is about 38.5x, suggesting the abstract likely conflates cost ratio with input-token ratio. Preserve the detailed values and do not repeat the 38x token claim without correction.

The ACRA repository publicly contains data/benchmark_translation.xlsx (13,782 bytes) and notebooks/Figures.ipynb. The notebook loads Sheet1, drops missing values, groups by metric and source, and computes means/stds for the Fig. 4D translation comparison. The exact spreadsheet cells could not be read through the available GitHub connector because it rejects non-UTF-8 binary content. Therefore the direct critique-agent ablation remains verified qualitatively but its six exact metric deltas remain unresolved; no figure-digitization guesses were introduced.

candidate_mechanisms_new.mechanism: Measurement-bound verified result registry / claim-number provenance gate
candidate_mechanisms_new.evidence: AutoResearchClaw component ablation on 10 ARC-Bench topics, best-of-3 per configuration-topic. Full system: completion 10/10, quality 5.62, accept 3/10, no fabrication. Without Verification: completion 10/10, apparent quality 5.48, apparent accept 5/10, but manual audit found fabricated/unsupported measured values in 3 of those 5 accepted papers. The paper explicitly marks the score/acceptance as inflated.
candidate_mechanisms_new.interpretation: A validity gate should bind reported quantitative claims to an immutable measurement registry rather than trusting fluent result analysis or paper-level reviewers. Removing the gate can make benchmark acceptance look better while scientific integrity worsens.
candidate_mechanisms_new.scope: Direct system-level causal ablation, small n=10 topics with best-of-3 selection; the verified registry prevents unlogged numbers but does not guarantee experiments answer the scientific question. A case study shows a zero-valued, semantically collapsed experiment can pass numeric verification because the measurements are genuine.

candidate_mechanisms_new.mechanism: Open-vs-closed reuse semantics: re-explore stochastic semantic operators; cache only closed deterministic artifacts under exact or certified equivalence
candidate_mechanisms_new.evidence: Eureka reports 50,000 repeated-search tasks where independent repeated open search succeeds 58.488% versus 24.492% when the first open-search output is forcibly memoized. On 30,000 adversarial surface-similar artifact pairs, approximate semantic merging makes 100% false merges while exact-identity/certified-equivalence merging makes 0%. Enabling deterministic runtime optimizations changes open-action ordering in 0/12,000 scientific frontiers.
candidate_mechanisms_new.interpretation: Long-horizon scientific agents should not apply ordinary memoization semantics to open hypothesis/search/reasoning operators. Reuse is safest for deterministic closure, exact structural identity, or explicitly certified equivalence, while open search should retain stochastic re-exploration capacity.
candidate_mechanisms_new.scope: Very large controlled systems ablations, but largely synthetic/runtime task suites from one research report; transfer to real scientific discovery quality is not yet independently established.

candidate_mechanisms_new.evidence: Eureka's governed-evolution comparison reports median total cost 2525.4 and success 60.55%, versus No Evolution 2686.8/58.09%, Always Evolve 3637.7/58.83%, and Evolve on Stall 2860.1/58.00%; EvolutionLease reduces median evolution round trips 12 to 4 and evolution-control cost 11.5%. Its architecture-promotion ablation additionally reports a cost-aware lazy policy with 0.04% false promotion and median execution cost 2277.13, versus complexity-only 14.90% false promotion; a cost-optimal reference is 2262.65.
candidate_mechanisms_new.interpretation: Self-modification/specialization should be an explicit amortized planning action rather than unconditional, complexity-triggered, or stall-only. The remaining horizon and expected reuse of the specialization matter.
candidate_mechanisms_new.scope: Direct within-system control-policy ablations, but evaluation task suites are controlled/synthetic and final scientific discoveries are not all externally validated.

negative_and_boundary_evidence_new: AutoResearchClaw's ARC-Bench comparison controls model backbone (GPT-5.3-codex), sandbox, and per-experiment time budget across frameworks, strengthening architecture-level attribution for experiment-stage scores. Its strict judge is still rubric-assisted agent evaluation; human cross-validation of judge leaves does not make it equivalent to independent scientific peer review.

AutoResearchClaw's cross-domain advantage is heavily confounded by domain-skill/software availability: AIDE-ML and AI Scientist v2 score zero in HEP/biology because required packages are unavailable, so those numbers should not be used as clean evidence of superior scientific reasoning.

AutoResearchClaw verification is necessary but not sufficient. Its T10 Full-Auto run passes numeric grounding because all recorded zero values are real, yet the experiment semantically collapses and fails to distinguish the eight CV strategies. Evidence provenance must be paired with evidence adequacy/discriminative experimental design.

The AutoResearchClaw HITL study shows non-monotonic intervention: CoPilot targeted six stages and reports 7.27 mean quality/87.5% accept over valid outputs, while Step-by-Step has 23 interventions and 5.19/50%; however validity denominators differ and the payload is human expertise, so this does not directly prove an autonomous model-escalation policy.

Eureka's reported scientific outputs should not be treated as externally established discoveries. The paper labels its RH result a certificate candidate rather than an RH proof and states that some theory results still require external or formal review.
Eureka's 170/170 recursive-task and large runtime-ablation results establish internal orchestration/correctness behavior on its benchmark suites, not publication-level scientific validity.

MLReplicate's abstract-level 38-fold input-token statement is inconsistent with the detailed resource figures; the 38.5x ratio matches monetary cost ($17.72 vs $0.46), while detailed input-token values imply about 840x between AI Researcher and CycleResearcher.

termination_diagnostics.additional_unresolved_frontier_action_be: After the ACRA artifact path established that the raw XLSX existed but could not be decoded through the UTF-8-only connector, the run did not stop.
